newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close higher, seen firm.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close higher, seen firm.

text.p: Argentine stocks continued their recovery from recent heavy losses Wednesday, driven by a rally in ADRs on Wall Street, dealers said.

"The market soaked up midsession profit-taking carried out by speculators and closed firm, boosted by purchases in leading blue chips by institutional investors like the AFJPs (private pension funds)," said Nestor de Cessare at traders Allaria Ledesma.
The blue-chip MerVal index rose 1.0 percent to 821.70, building on Tuesday's 2.9 percent jump, which snapped a sharp losing spell.
"The market will seesaw higher trying to reach its all-time high of 890, but we will have to keep a close eye on developments in Brazil," another dealer said.

Traders blamed last week's dive of nearly six percent on devaluation fears in Brazil, although they also noted the bolsa was heading for a correction after rising almost 30 percent this year to a five-year-high of 857.32.

Floor volume picked up to 39.4 million pesos from 36.2 million Tuesday, while over-the-counter turnover soared to 231.4 million pesos from 164.6 million Tuesday on strong institutional buys, dealers said.
The broad market closed up 1.8 percent, with winners pounding losers 56 to 18 and 16 issues closing flat.
The top main-tier gainers were construction stock Polledo, oil company Astra and Telecom, which shot up 5.6 percent, 4.4 percent and 3.4 percent, respectively.
MerVal losers were led by steelmaker Acindar, electricity generator Central Puerto and gas distributor Transportadora de Gas del Sur, off 3.5 percent, 2.7 percent and 1.3 percent, respectively.
